chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhariyy from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abi al-'Azrami from his father, who raised the hadith to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who said:
One who leads a people in prayer while among them is someone more knowledgeable and more juristically proficient than him, their affair shall remain in a low/base state until the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a less knowledgeable person leading prayer when a more learned scholar is present?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* establishes the principle of *al-awla bi-l-amr* (the most worthy takes charge) in communal leadership, specifically highlighting the spiritual detriment of a less qualified individual assuming authority over a more learned jurist (*faqih*). It underscores the Shia emphasis on scholarly hierarchy, warning that such misalignment leads to a perpetual state of *safal* (lowliness or deficiency) in the community's affairs until the Day of Judgment.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “One who assumes the responsibility of the community in spite of the presence of learned scholars  and jurists, shall be  in the  base level (of Hell).”
